name: Nile Rodgers
hook: Chic's guitarist and co-writer, whose 'Good Times' became the first hit rap record's backing track and who then produced Bowie and Madonna's biggest records.
blurb: Nile Rodgers was born on the Lower East Side of Manhattan in 1952. With the bass player Bernard Edwards he formed Chic in 1977, out of the Big Apple Band: a disco band known for tight, choppy rhythm guitar and melodic bass. 'Le Freak' (1978) was Atlantic's first triple-platinum single, and 'Good Times' followed in 1979. That year the Sugarhill Gang's 'Rapper's Delight' was built on 'Good Times' without asking. Rodgers and Edwards threatened legal action and got their names added as co-writers, which Rodgers has called the one time he objected to his work being used. He went on to produce David Bowie's 'Let's Dance' (1983) and Madonna's 'Like a Virgin' (1984), carrying Chic's rhythm-section style into 1980s pop, and in 2013 he played on Daft Punk's 'Get Lucky'.
